title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
summary: 단일 쿼리로 학습한 on-policy distillation이 전체 데이터셋 학습의 대부분의 이득을 회복하며, 상태 커버리지 분석을 통해 OPD가 데이터 과잉 공급이지만 알고리즘 부족 상태임을 보여준다.
reason: A well-executed empirical study that challenges a common assumption about on-policy distillation—that large amounts of training data are necessary. The state-coverage framework provides a useful lens for understanding OPD's data efficiency, and the finding that one query reaches 71.5% of full-data state coverage is concrete and actionable. The evaluation is honest (acknowledging that alignment remains slow regardless of data volume) and extends to multiple settings (multi-teacher OPD, off-domain queries). However, the contribution is primarily analytical rather than methodological—it explains existing behavior rather than proposing a new technique that practitioners would immediately adopt. The practical impact depends on whether practitioners can exploit these insights to improve OPD efficiency, which the paper does not fully demonstrate.
author: Zixuan Fu, Bingxiang He, Yuxin Zuo, Haohuan Huang, Jinqian Zhang

title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
summary: SWE-Gate는 기능 테스트 통과만으로는 부족하다는 점을 보여주는 소프트웨어 엔지니어링 에이전트 벤치마크로, 실제 코드 리뷰 제약 조건을 명시적으로 평가하며 303개의 저장소 수준 수리 인스턴스를 통해 기능적 성공과 리뷰 제약 준수 사이의 상당한 격차를 드러낸다.
reason: SWE-Gate addresses a genuine gap in how we evaluate coding agents: existing benchmarks measure functional correctness but ignore real-world acceptance criteria from code review. The benchmark construction is solid (303 instances from 75 repos with review-derived constraints), and the empirical finding is meaningful—34% of functionally correct patches fail review constraints. This would change how practitioners evaluate agents for production use. However, the contribution is primarily a benchmark and evaluation framework rather than a new method or capability. The paper lacks depth on what specific constraint types matter most or how agents could be improved to handle them, limiting its impact on practitioners building systems.
author: Xin He, Yanlin Wang, Mingwei Liu, Jiachi Chen, Hongyu Zhang

title: From Deceptive Outputs to Deceptive Mechanisms: A Causal Framework for Language-Model Deception Research
summary: 언어 모델의 기만 행동에 대한 연구에서 인간의 정신 상태 개념을 부적절하게 적용하는 문제를 지적하며, 기만적으로 보이는 출력과 실제 기만 메커니즘을 구분하는 인과 분류체계를 제시하고, 제어된 실험을 통해 기만적 행동이 제안된 메커니즘 없이도 발생할 수 있음을 보여준다.
reason: This paper makes a valuable conceptual contribution to an important and often-confused area of AI safety research. It introduces a rigorous causal framework that disambiguates between deceptive outputs and deceptive mechanisms—a distinction that is frequently blurred in popular discourse and research. The work tests these distinctions empirically across two model families with controlled experiments (guessing games, stock trading), providing concrete evidence that deceptive-looking behavior can arise without the proposed underlying mechanisms. The causal taxonomy is well-articulated and addresses a real methodological problem in the field. However, the scope is somewhat narrow (two model families, specific experimental domains), and the paper does not propose new methods to prevent deception or demonstrate findings that would directly change practitioner behavior in model deployment. The contribution is primarily conceptual clarity and negative results (showing what deceptive behavior does NOT imply), which is valuable for research rigor but not a capability advance.
author: Yakov Pyotr Shkolnikov

title: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
summary: 기존 에이전트 궤적(trajectory)에서 파일 작업 기록을 재생하여 실행 가능한 환경을 복원하고, 이를 통해 새로운 작업을 합성하는 Terminal-Universe 프레임워크를 제안하며, 37.3k개의 작업 환경을 생성하여 Qwen3.5-27B의 성능을 Terminal-Bench와 EvoCode-Bench에서 각각 11.9점, 13.8점 향상시켰다.
reason: A solid contribution that addresses a real bottleneck in agent training: the scarcity of executable environments. The core insight—reconstructing environments from agent trajectories—is sensible and well-motivated. The paper demonstrates concrete value through scale (37.3k environments) and measurable improvements on established benchmarks (11.9 and 13.8 point gains). The approach combines trajectory replay, completion agents, and task synthesis in a coherent framework. However, the evaluation is limited to fine-tuning results on two benchmarks without ablations or analysis of environment reconstruction quality, and there is no discussion of failure modes or limitations. The work is reproducible in principle but depends on access to the original trajectories and the completion agent's behavior. This is a useful engineering contribution that practitioners building terminal agents would benefit from, but it lacks the depth of analysis or breakthrough results needed for a higher tier.
author: Jie Wu, Zhenru Zhang, Beichen Zhang, Xuwu Wang, Yuhui Su

title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
summary: OPD-then-RL 순차 구성이 OPD와 RLVR의 가중합이나 rescaling 같은 결합 방식보다 논리 및 수학 추론에서 일관되게 우수하며, OPD가 teacher 지원 해법의 커버리지를 확장하고 RL이 그 범위 내에서 예측을 날카롭게 하는 상호보완적 역할을 한다는 것을 보여준다.
reason: A solid empirical contribution with clear practical value. The paper demonstrates that sequential application of on-policy distillation followed by RL consistently outperforms joint optimization across multiple benchmarks. The analysis provides useful mechanistic insight (coverage expansion vs. sharpening) and actionable guidance (using OPD validation score as switching signal). The evaluation covers logic and math reasoning tasks with appropriate baselines. However, the core contribution is primarily empirical ordering of existing methods rather than a novel technique, and the scope is limited to reasoning tasks. The work would change how practitioners combine these two post-training approaches, but the novelty is moderate.
author: Boyan Li, Bingsen Chen, Chenghao Yang, Ping Nie, Chen Zhao

title: Why Gated DeltaNet Survives 4-Bit Quantization: NVFP4 W4A4 for the Recurrent Half of a Hybrid 27B LLM
summary: Hybrid LLM의 선형 어텐션 부분(Gated DeltaNet)이 4비트 양자화에 견디는 이유를 실증적으로 분석하고, NVFP4 W4A4 양자화를 모든 496개 선형 레이어에 적용한 Minima 모델이 BF16 기준선과 동등한 성능을 유지하면서 더 작고 빠름을 보여준다.
reason: A solid empirical contribution with thorough evaluation and practical value. The paper challenges a common assumption (that recurrent layers need higher precision) with convincing evidence across multiple benchmarks. The mechanistic analysis explaining why GDN survives 4-bit quantization is valuable, and the released checkpoint adds reproducibility. However, the scope is somewhat narrow (one model architecture, one quantization scheme), and the gains, while consistent, are incremental rather than transformative. The work would change deployment decisions for practitioners using hybrid LLMs, but doesn't establish a fundamentally new capability.
author: Sergii Kozyrev, Davyd Maiboroda

title: PatchBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Vulnerability Patching
summary: AI 에이전트의 취약점 패칭 평가에서 패치 암기와 표면 수준의 수정이라는 두 가지 주요 문제를 식별하고, 이를 해결하기 위해 PatchBench 벤치마크를 제안하며, 기존 PoC 기반 검증이 성공률을 평균 1.83배 과장한다는 것을 보여준다.
reason: This paper makes a solid empirical contribution by identifying and quantifying real validity threats in vulnerability patching evaluation. The finding that 25% of agent patches memorize historical patches and that PoC-only validation inflates success rates by 1.83× is concrete and actionable. The proposed benchmark with transplant and mutation techniques is a reasonable methodological improvement. However, the scope is narrow (C/C++ only), the paper is primarily a benchmark/evaluation contribution rather than a new method, and the abstract does not indicate whether the benchmark or code will be released. The work would be valuable for practitioners building or evaluating patching agents, but does not represent a breakthrough capability or fundamental advance.
author: Chihao Shen, Jiacheng Li, Aastha Mahajan, Jeffery Siyuan Tian, Yonghwi Kwon

title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
summary: LLM 기반 코드 수정에서 모델이 필요 이상으로 코드를 재작성하는 '과도한 편집' 현상을 체계적으로 분석하고, 보존 지시문과 강화학습을 통해 이를 완화할 수 있음을 보여주는 연구.
reason: This paper identifies and systematically studies a real problem in LLM-based code editing—over-editing—that practitioners should care about. The evaluation framework is well-designed with controlled AST-level corruptions and known minimal patches, providing honest measurement. The findings are concrete: over-editing is widespread even in strong models, and the paper demonstrates both prompt-based and training-based mitigations with clear trade-offs. The work is reproducible in scope (uses public benchmarks) and addresses a practical concern for code repair systems. However, the contribution is somewhat narrow—it focuses on a specific quality dimension rather than a fundamentally new capability—and the improvements, while meaningful, are modest (2.3 points Pass@1 gain). The paper makes a solid empirical contribution but lacks the breadth or magnitude of impact for a higher tier.
author: Tongyao Zhu, Wei Hern Lim, Min-Yen Kan

title: Representational alignment yields generalizable safety in language models
summary: 이 논문은 인지과학의 프로토타입 이론에 기반하여 LLM의 내부 표현 구조를 인간의 도덕 판단과 정렬시키는 representational similarity optimization을 제안하며, 표준 행동 정렬 방식보다 적대적 공격에 대한 견고성이 더 일관되게 향상됨을 23개 모델과 25만 개 이상의 도덕 주석을 통해 입증했다.
reason: This paper presents a well-motivated approach to LLM safety grounded in cognitive science (prototype theory) and demonstrates a clear empirical finding: representational alignment improves adversarial robustness more consistently than standard behavioral alignment, despite more modest gains on explicit benchmarks. The evaluation is reasonably thorough (23 models, 251k annotations, multiple attack strategies), and the core insight—that internal representation structure matters for generalization—is valuable for practitioners building robust systems. However, the practical impact remains somewhat uncertain: the adversarial robustness gains, while consistent, are not quantified in detail in the abstract, and it's unclear how large they are relative to other defense approaches. The work is honest about trade-offs (explicit performance vs. robustness) and the method appears reproducible, but the scope is focused on a specific safety angle rather than a breakthrough capability.
author: Lingyu Li, Yan Teng, Yingchun Wang, Xia Hu

title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
summary: Chain-of-thought 추론 단계의 텍스트가 그 기능적 중요도를 실제로 인코딩하는지 검토하는 논문으로, Monte Carlo 롤아웃을 통해 정의한 단계 중요도(advantage)를 기준으로 LLM 판사의 성능을 평가하여, 현재의 프로세스 보상 모델과 CoT 감독 방법이 추론 추적의 가독성을 해석가능성으로 잘못 취급할 수 있음을 보여준다.
reason: This paper addresses a practically important gap between the legibility and actual interpretability of chain-of-thought reasoning—a distinction that directly affects how practitioners should use LLM judges, process reward models, and reasoning supervision. The evaluation is methodologically sound: the authors operationalize step importance via Monte Carlo rollouts (a principled ground truth), measure whether LLM judges can recover it, and quantify the gap between performance and a noise ceiling. The finding that LLMs fall short of ceiling even after fine-tuning is a useful negative result that should temper confidence in current CoT-based supervision methods. The work is honest about limitations and directly challenges assumptions embedded in popular techniques. However, the scope is somewhat narrow (focused on step-level importance in CoT), the evaluation is limited to a subset of reasoning tasks, and the paper does not propose a solution—it primarily diagnoses a problem. This makes it high-value for practitioners building on CoT and reward modeling, but not a must-read that changes the field.
author: Kevin Du, Alexander Hoyle, Laura Ruis, Acyr Locatelli

title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
summary: 이 논문은 discrete diffusion을 활용하여 LLM의 자동회귀 생성을 병렬화하는 diffusion-augmented LLM을 제안하며, 기존 AR 모델의 품질을 유지하면서 최대 3배의 추론 속도 향상을 달성한다.
reason: A solid contribution addressing a real bottleneck in LLM inference. The core idea—using discrete diffusion to generate multiple tokens in parallel while preserving an underlying autoregressive model—is well-motivated and appears novel. The evaluation is reasonably comprehensive (throughput, quality benchmarks, comparisons to speculative decoding and diffusion baselines), and the authors release code and checkpoints, supporting reproducibility. However, the abstract does not provide sufficient detail on the magnitude of quality-speed tradeoffs, ablation studies, or theoretical justification for why this approach should work. The claimed 3× speedup and outperformance of larger models (26B DiffusionGemma with an 8B model) are noteworthy but would benefit from more granular reporting. The method's practical impact depends on whether the speedups hold across diverse workloads and whether the training overhead of diffusion distillation is truly negligible—details not evident from the abstract alone.
author: Subham Sekhar Sahoo, Lingjie Chen, Khiem Pham, Jonathan Geuter, Chaitanya Dwivedi

title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
summary: 온라인 3D 재구성에서 장시간 비디오에 대한 누적 포즈 드리프트 문제를 해결하기 위해, 고정된 백본에 경량 학습 가능 토큰을 주입하여 다중 과거 키프레임 기준의 상대 포즈를 쿼리하는 Scal3R을 제안하며, 포즈 그래프 최적화와 루프 클로저를 통해 KITTI에서 60% 이상의 ATE 감소를 달성한다.
reason: Solid contribution addressing a real problem in online 3D reconstruction. The core insight—that per-frame depth remains stable while pose regression fails on long sequences—is well-motivated and leads to a practical solution. Multi-reference relative pose querying with frozen backbone and lightweight learnable tokens is a sensible design. Strong empirical results across multiple benchmarks (60% ATE reduction on KITTI, SOTA on 5 other datasets) with reasonable computational efficiency (8 hours single GPU). However, the novelty is somewhat incremental—relative pose estimation and pose-graph optimization are established techniques; the main contribution is their combination with efficient attention-based querying. Limited details in abstract about ablation studies, failure cases, or how the approach compares to other recent online reconstruction methods. The work would benefit practitioners building 3D reconstruction systems, but doesn't represent a fundamental breakthrough.
author: Chin-Yang Lin, Yang-Che Sun, Cheng Sun, Fu-En Yang, Min-Hung Chen

title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
summary: 생성 비디오에서 물리 추론을 평가하기 위해 보정 불필요한 관계적 일관성 기반 벤치마크 Principia를 제안하며, 최신 비디오 생성 모델들이 기존 지표에서는 높은 점수를 받지만 물리 법칙 준수에서는 심각하게 실패함을 보여준다.
reason: Solid contribution addressing a real gap in video model evaluation. The relational physics approach is clever—using paired object consistency to avoid calibration dependencies is a genuine insight that makes physics testing practical for generated video. The benchmark spans meaningful phenomena and the evaluation is honest: showing that SOTA models fail despite high scores on existing metrics (VBench) is valuable negative evidence. However, the scope is narrow (physics only), and the paper's impact depends on whether practitioners adopt this evaluation approach. The work would be stronger with deeper analysis of failure modes and clearer guidance on what models should do differently.
author: Varun Varma Thozhiyoor, Shivam Tripathi, Venkatesh Babu Radhakrishnan, Anand Bhattad

title: Persistent Identity Preservation in Generative Image Models: A Benchmark and Evaluation System
summary: 생성 이미지 모델에서 특정 대상의 정체성을 유지하는 문제를 체계적으로 평가하는 벤치마크를 제시하며, 입력 컨텍스트, 학습 가능한 파라미터, 지속적 정체성 레이어 등 세 가지 패러다임을 비교하여 정체성 보존이 단순히 모델 성능 향상만으로는 달성되지 않음을 보여준다.
reason: This paper addresses a genuine practical problem in generative image models—identity preservation across edits and variations—with a systematic benchmark and evaluation framework. The contribution is primarily empirical: a well-designed evaluation system that compares three distinct architectural paradigms (input context, trainable parameters, persistent layers) across multiple challenging scenarios. The finding that identity preservation doesn't automatically improve with model capability is valuable for practitioners. However, the novelty is limited to benchmarking and evaluation rather than proposing fundamentally new methods; the persistent identity approach (PHOTA IDENTITY) is mentioned but not deeply explored. The paper would be stronger with released code, detailed ablations, or quantitative metrics beyond what the abstract suggests. The work is solid and useful for the community building identity-aware generation systems, but falls short of being a must-read breakthrough.
author: Mengwei Ren, Xuaner Zhang, Zhihao Xia

title: DSAQuant: Denoising-Stage-Aligned Quantization-Aware Training for Video Generation
summary: 비디오 확산 모델의 양자화 인식 훈련에서 기존 방법들이 세부 사항과 텍스처 품질을 심각하게 저하시키는 문제를 해결하기 위해, 노이징 제거 단계의 서로 다른 기능(초기 단계는 구조, 후기 단계는 세부 사항)에 맞춘 DSAQuant 프레임워크를 제안한다.
reason: A solid contribution addressing a real problem in video diffusion model deployment. The paper identifies a genuine limitation of existing QAT methods (timestep-agnostic quantization) and proposes a principled solution (stage-aligned training and inference). The evaluation is reasonably comprehensive across two model families and multiple quantization settings, with meaningful improvements (6.60 VBench points under W3A3). The insight about stage-wise denoising functionality is intuitive and well-motivated. However, the scope is somewhat narrow (video generation only), and the paper lacks comparison to other recent VDM compression approaches beyond QAT baselines. No mention of code or model release limits reproducibility. The work would be valuable for practitioners deploying video models but doesn't represent a breakthrough in quantization methodology.
author: Shuaiting Li, Zelin Gao, Haibin Shen, Yujun Shen, Haotong Qin

title: Stable and Scalable Bundle Adjustment of Holistic 3D Structures
summary: Bundle adjustment 프레임워크를 확장하여 점과 선뿐만 아니라 평행성, 공면성 등의 고차 기하학적 관계를 함께 최적화하면서도 고전적인 점 기반 BA와 비슷한 계산 성능을 유지하는 방법을 제안한다.
reason: A solid technical contribution that addresses a real problem in 3D vision: extending bundle adjustment to handle richer geometric structures (lines, parallelism, coplanarity, wireframes) while maintaining computational efficiency and numerical stability. The key insight—modeling group constraints as camera-like entities and expressing them through 2D reprojection errors—is clever and appears well-motivated. The claimed preservation of sparsity structure under Schur elimination is valuable for practitioners. However, the abstract provides limited evidence of the magnitude of improvements: 'significantly richer' and 'improved accuracy' lack quantitative support. The evaluation scope is unclear (which datasets, which baselines for comparison). The work is technically sound and addresses a genuine bottleneck in structure-from-motion pipelines, but without stronger empirical validation or released code mentioned, it falls short of 'must read' territory.

title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
summary: EditVid는 sparse causal memory, correspondence 기반 token injection, soft latent blending을 결합한 학습 불필요 프레임워크로, instruction-guided와 reference-guided 비디오 편집을 통합 지원하며 FiVE 벤치마크에서 기존 방법 대비 크게 향상된 성능을 보인다.

The breadth of supported tasks (style transfer, attribute modification, object insertion, part-level editing, subject replacement) is valuable for practitioners, but the abstract does not clarify which tasks show the largest gains or whether all achieve competitive performance. No mention of code or model release limits reproducibility. The work is competent and useful for video editing applications, but does not represent a breakthrough capability or settle a fundamental question in the field.

reason: The paper addresses a genuine gap between principled but intractable causal explanation methods (actual causality) and scalable but theoretically loose attribution methods (SHAP). The contribution is solid in scope but the evaluation evidence presented is thin. Practitioners building explainability systems would find this interesting, but the abstract does not demonstrate that PCI substantially outperforms or meaningfully changes how they should approach causal explanation in deployed settings.

title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-AI Interaction
summary: 이 논문은 반복적인 인간-AI 상호작용 데이터를 활용하여 테스트 시간에 AI 에이전트를 개인 사용자에게 적응시키는 TAHI(test-time adaptation through human-agent interaction) 방법을 제안하며, 쓰기와 시각 창작 도메인에서 30명의 사용자를 대상으로 600개 작업에 대해 평가하여 수십 개 작업 내에서 4.5-20.9%의 성공률 개선을 달성했다.

title: Epistemic Warrant for LLM Recommendations: Characterizing the Basis for Reliance When Ground Truth Is Unavailable
summary: LLM 권장사항의 신뢰성을 개별 결정 수준에서 평가하기 위해 인식론적 기초를 바탕으로 '인식론적 정당성(epistemic warrant)'을 도입하고, 모델 선호도의 안정성과 적용 범위를 특징짓는 4단계 인증 체계를 제시한다.
reason: This paper addresses a genuine practical problem—how to assess whether to trust individual LLM recommendations when ground truth is unavailable—and proposes a theoretically motivated framework. The validation approach (known-groups tests, crowd consensus) is reasonable but modest in scope. The contribution is solid conceptually but the evaluation is limited to pairwise recommendations and relatively small-scale validation. The work would be useful for practitioners building systems that rely on LLM recommendations, but the evidence for the framework's real-world utility remains preliminary. No code or data release is mentioned. The paper makes a meaningful but incremental contribution to an important problem rather than a breakthrough result.
author: Shai Vardi, João Sedoc

title: Adaptive Vision-Language Grasping via Composable Foundation Priors and Generalizable Grasp Synthesis
summary: AdaRoboVLG는 기초 모델의 작업 이해를 물리적 파지 합성으로부터 분리하여, 재학습 없이 다양한 로봇 손에 걸쳐 적응형 파지를 가능하게 하는 비전-언어-파지 프레임워크를 제안한다.
reason: A solid contribution to robotic grasping that demonstrates a useful architectural principle—decoupling physical grasp synthesis from task-dependent understanding via foundation models. The paper shows convincing cross-hand generalization and addresses multiple grasping challenges (spatial, cognitive, temporal priors). However, the evaluation is limited to simulation and unspecified real-world experiments without detailed quantitative comparisons to current strong baselines. The core idea of composable priors is reasonable but not novel in isolation. The work would be stronger with rigorous benchmarking against recent vision-language grasping methods and clearer evidence that the modular approach outperforms end-to-end alternatives by a meaningful margin.
author: Sixu Yan, Shikang Wang, Binhua Huang, Xuanlai Tang, Guohua Fan

title: DRACO: Fine-Grained Credit Assignment with Dynamic Rubrics for Long-Horizon Agent Training
summary: DRACO는 장기 에이전트 학습에서 지상 진실 보상 없이 동적으로 생성된 루브릭을 궤적 수준에서 평가한 후 폐쇄형 재분배를 통해 단계별 이점으로 변환하여 신용 할당 문제를 해결한다.
reason: DRACO addresses a real problem in long-horizon RL—credit assignment without ground-truth rewards—with a reasonable approach: dynamic rubric generation and closed-form redistribution of trajectory-level scores to per-step advantages. The empirical results show consistent gains on two benchmarks (AppWorld and Tau-Bench), and the method avoids training additional attribution modules. However, the evaluation is limited to two domains, the improvements over GRPO with sparse rewards are modest (5.3 points on Tau-Bench), and the paper does not compare against other recent credit-assignment methods in long-horizon settings. The contribution is solid but narrow in scope, and it remains unclear how well the approach generalizes beyond these specific benchmarks or how sensitive it is to rubric quality and design choices.
author: Shubham Gandhi, Saurabh Goyal, Kiran Kate, Yara Rizk

title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation
summary: CORE는 MLLM 기반 임베딩 모델의 합성적 추론(compositional reasoning) 능력을 개선하기 위해 크로스-어텐션 리랭커의 판단을 임베딩 모델으로 증류하는 방법을 제안하며, Rank-KL 목적함수와 다단계 감독을 통해 COLA, SUGARCREPE++, NEGBENCH에서 기존 모델을 크게 앞지른다.
reason: A solid contribution addressing a real limitation in multimodal embedding models—compositional reasoning—with a well-motivated approach (distilling reranker judgments into embeddings) and comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks. The work introduces useful methodological elements (graded evaluation protocol, Rank-KL objective, multi-level candidate synthesis) and demonstrates consistent improvements. However, the scope is narrow (focused on a specific failure mode of MLLM embeddings), the gains, while substantial on compositional benchmarks, come with limited analysis of why the approach works, and the practical impact for practitioners building retrieval systems depends on whether compositional reasoning is a bottleneck in their use case. The paper is well-executed within its scope but does not represent a fundamental shift in how practitioners should approach multimodal retrieval.
author: Tingyu Song, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Chu Liu

title: TAP-Path: Task-Adaptive Structural and Token Pruning for Efficient and Trustworthy Pathology Foundation Models
summary: TAP-Path는 Virchow2 pathology foundation model을 구조적 및 토큰 pruning으로 압축하여 파라미터 25%, 계산량 35% 감소시키면서 신뢰성 지표를 유지하는 작업 적응형 압축 프레임워크를 제시한다.
reason: A solid contribution to an important practical problem—making large pathology models efficient—with reasonable technical approach and comprehensive evaluation. However, the core novelty is limited (combining known pruning techniques), the accuracy drop versus full Virchow2 is non-trivial (~1%), and the work is narrowly scoped to one model and domain. The evaluation is honest and includes useful reliability metrics, but lacks comparison to other compression baselines (distillation, quantization) that would clarify the method's standing. Useful for practitioners deploying pathology models under compute constraints, but not a methodological advance that changes how the field approaches model compression.
author: Mehedi Hasan, Ashfak Yeafi, Md Khairul Islam

reason: A solid contribution to an important problem (sample efficiency in RLHF reward learning) with a reasonable technical approach (subspace EKF for uncertainty quantification). The paper demonstrates improvements in sample efficiency, runtime, and calibration on established benchmarks (D4RL, V-D4RL) with released code. However, the scope is narrow—focused on a specific component of RLHF rather than end-to-end capability gains—and the abstract does not provide evidence of breakthrough performance or invalidation of prior assumptions. The work is technically sound but incremental within active reward learning.
author: Yutai Zhou, Erdem Bıyık

title: Spurious Advantage Hidden in GRPO
summary: GRPO의 advantage estimator가 정답에 도달한 추론과 우연한 추측을 구분하지 못하는 문제를 지적하고, 검증자 부호와 전역 스케일을 사용하는 SIGNBALANCE를 제안하는 논문이다.
reason: The paper identifies a real failure mode in GRPO's advantage estimation—spurious rewards for guessing—and proposes a targeted fix. The problem is well-motivated with concrete examples (bounded answers, open-answer subsets, search agents). However, the evaluation is limited: improvements are modest and inconsistent (matches GRPO on open-answer math, improves on bounded-answer and search), no comparison to other recent RL methods beyond GRPO, and no ablation study details provided in the abstract. The contribution is narrow (a fix to one algorithm's advantage estimator) rather than a fundamental insight. Code availability would strengthen reproducibility but is only promised. For practitioners using GRPO on bounded-answer tasks, this is useful; for the broader RL community, the impact is incremental.
author: Jiamian Wang, Samyadeep Basu, Koustava Goswami, Tong Yu, Zhiqiang Tao

title: FLY-EVAL++: An Evidence-Driven Evaluation Protocol for Safety-Constrained Flight Prediction with Large Language Models
summary: 안전-제약 조건이 있는 비행 궤적 예측에서 LLM을 평가하기 위해 정확도 이상의 메트릭이 필요하다는 점을 인식하고, 프로토콜 준수, 물리적 타당성, 안전 제약을 검증하는 FLY-EVAL++ 평가 프로토콜을 제안한다.
reason: This paper addresses a real problem—evaluating LLMs in safety-critical domains requires more than accuracy metrics—and proposes a structured evaluation protocol with concrete instantiation on flight prediction. The work demonstrates meaningful findings (safety compliance as a discriminative dimension, 28-point gaps between models with similar accuracy). However, the contribution is primarily methodological and domain-specific. The evaluation is limited to flight prediction tasks, and while the protocol design is sound, it is not clear whether the insights generalize beyond this narrow application or whether the protocol itself represents a significant advance over existing safety evaluation frameworks. The paper would be stronger with evidence that this protocol catches failure modes that other evaluation approaches miss, or with application to multiple safety-critical domains. The finding that LLMs fail on safety constraints even when numerically accurate is valuable but somewhat expected. Code and data availability are not mentioned in the abstract, limiting reproducibility.
author: Yalun Wu, Junfeng Fang, Jiawei Wang, Haotian Liu, Qijun Yang

title: InSituMeasure: Probing Situated Measurement Grounding in Industrial Scenes with Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: InSituMeasure는 산업 현장의 실제 계측 작업에서 MLLM의 신뢰성을 평가하기 위한 벤치마크로, 8개 카테고리의 전문 계측기 2,922개 장면을 포함하며 최고 성능 모델도 25.7% 정확도에 불과함을 보여준다.
reason: A solid benchmark contribution addressing a real gap in MLLM evaluation. InSituMeasure provides 2,922 annotated industrial scenes with realistic measurement tasks, revealing substantial performance gaps (25.7% accuracy) across 24 state-of-the-art models. The dataset design is thoughtful—including noise tags, unit consistency checks, and diagnostic annotations—and the failure analysis identifies concrete failure modes (text shortcuts, overconfidence, industrial noise). However, the contribution is primarily a benchmark rather than a novel method; the paper's value depends on whether practitioners will adopt it and whether the identified gaps motivate new approaches. The scope is narrow (measurement grounding in industrial settings) but well-motivated for practitioners building vision systems for real-world applications.
author: Chao Shen, Xinyuan Li, Yunfan Zhou, Jianguo Yao, Haibing Guan

title: Last Translation Benchmark
summary: Last Translation Benchmark는 포화 상태에 접어든 기계번역 벤치마크를 보완하기 위해 인간이 작성하고 검증한 어려운 사례들과 구체적인 실패 케이스를 기술하는 검증 규칙을 제시하는 라이브 데이터셋을 제안한다.
reason: The paper addresses a real problem—saturation of standard MT benchmarks and unreliability of automatic metrics—and proposes a thoughtful solution: adversarially-collected hard examples with handcrafted verification rules. The idea of moving beyond automatic metrics to structured failure-case evaluation is sound. However, the abstract provides no evidence of the benchmark's actual utility: no comparison of how well the verification rules work, no data on inter-rater reliability, no demonstration that this approach better identifies improvement pathways than existing methods, and no baseline results showing which models fail and why. The claim that this is a 'live dataset' accepting contributions is a design choice, not a validation. Without empirical evidence that the benchmark successfully differentiates models or that the verification rules are reliable and actionable, this reads as a well-motivated tool proposal rather than a validated contribution. Reproducibility depends on whether the benchmark and rules are released.
author: Vilém Zouhar, Niyati Bafna, Mukund Choudhary, Maike Züfle, Sara Rajaee

title: The Dice Roll Method: A Standardized Protocol for Repeated-Query Auditing of Large Language Model Brand Recommendations
summary: LLM 브랜드 추천의 반복 쿼리 감사를 위한 표준화된 프로토콜을 제안하며, 일반화 이론과 부트스트랩 기반 통계 방법론으로 반복 횟수(n=5~15)와 신뢰도 임계값을 결정하는 체계적 지침을 제공한다.
reason: A methodologically rigorous contribution to a narrow but important domain. The paper formalizes a standardized protocol for auditing LLM behavior with solid statistical grounding (generalizability theory, negative-binomial mixed models, bootstrap methods) and validates it across ~190k observations. However, the scope is limited to brand recommendations specifically, the practical impact on practitioners building with LLMs is unclear, and the core insight—that repeated queries need principled iteration counts and metrics—addresses a real but specialized auditing need rather than changing how models are built or deployed.
author: Dmitrij Żatuchin

title: Robust PAC Learning of Concurrent Stochastic Games
summary: 일반합 동시 확률 게임(concurrent stochastic games)에 대한 첫 번째 PAC 학습 프레임워크를 제시하며, Nash 균형 존재 여부를 판단하는 Nash margin 특성화를 통해 근사 균형 또는 균형 부재 증명서를 반환한다.
reason: A solid theoretical contribution to multi-agent reinforcement learning with novel elements (Nash margin characterization, robust PAC framework for CSGs), but limited practical impact. The work addresses a well-defined problem with rigorous analysis and polynomial sample complexity guarantees. However, the scope is narrow (concurrent stochastic games with specific assumptions), empirical validation is on benchmarks only, and the practical applicability for practitioners building systems remains unclear. The Nash margin idea is interesting but the overall contribution is primarily theoretical rather than enabling new capabilities.
author: Angel Y. He, David Parker

title: Parameterised graph theory for tensor networks: entanglement rerouting, structural simplification, and agnostic tomography
summary: 매개변수화된 그래프 이론을 사용하여 텐서 네트워크 상태의 MPS/TTN 표현 가능성과 학습 복잡도를 cutwidth, tree-cutwidth 등의 그래프 매개변수로 특성화하고, 얽힘 재라우팅 기법과 확장된 학습 알고리즘을 통해 표본 및 계산 복잡도 상한을 도출한다.
reason: This paper makes solid theoretical contributions connecting parameterised graph theory to tensor network learning and representation, with rigorous proofs and extensions to new settings (TTNs, arbitrary graphs, agnostic learning). However, the work is primarily theoretical with limited empirical validation, addresses a specialized domain (tensor network simulation), and the practical impact for practitioners building with neural networks or large-scale models remains unclear. The results are well-evidenced within their scope but the scope itself is narrow.
author: Matthias C. Caro, Natalie McHugh, Sergii Strelchuk

title: Prospective Coding Improves Learning in Deep Continuous-Time Recurrent Networks
summary: 심층 연속시간 순환신경망에서 시간 적분으로 인한 신호 지연과 오차 감쇠 문제를 해결하기 위해 생물학적으로 영감받은 복소수 값 시간 필터인 Recursive Quadrature Filters (RQFs)와 예측적 입력 코딩을 제안하며, 여러 모델과 학습 방식에서 평가한다.
reason: A solid contribution with clear technical novelty (RQFs and prospective coding) and reasonable evaluation across multiple architectures. However, the practical impact is limited by narrow scope (speech and synthetic tasks), modest improvements over baselines, and lack of comparison to current strong alternatives like Transformers or recent SSM variants. The biological motivation and theoretical grounding are interesting but don't translate to compelling empirical advantages that would change practitioner decisions.
author: Shivang Rawat, Mirko Morello, Flaviano Morone, David J. Heeger

title: Constant regret in general games via higher-order optimism
summary: N-player 일반 게임에서 상수 후회(constant regret)를 달성하는 고차 낙관주의 기반의 비결합 학습 알고리즘 HOOD를 제시하며, O(N³log²K) 개별 후회 보장을 제공한다.
reason: This paper makes a solid theoretical contribution to multi-player game theory by achieving constant regret bounds in general N-player games—a known open problem. The result is non-trivial: the O(N³log²K) bound improves significantly over concurrent work (O(N²¹log⁴K)), and the algorithmic approach (HOOD) combines higher-order optimism with discounting in a principled way. However, the contribution is narrowly scoped to theoretical regret analysis with no empirical validation, no code release mentioned, and unclear practical implications for practitioners building systems. The paper advances our theoretical understanding but does not demonstrate that this insight changes how one would build or deploy learning systems in practice.
author: Omar Abbadi, Rida Laraki, Panayotis Mertikopoulos

title: Hardware-Aware FP4 FlashAttention-4
summary: Blackwell GPU의 FP4 텐서 코어가 softmax 변환과 온칩 의존성으로 인해 attention을 자동으로 가속화하지 못하는 문제를 해결하기 위해 Direct-P 방법을 제안하며, noncausal 추론에서 BF16 대비 최대 2.13배, 8B 모델 학습에서 최대 1.14배 속도 향상을 달성한다.
reason: A focused optimization paper addressing a real hardware-software mismatch on Blackwell GPUs. The contribution is narrow but concrete: showing that FP4 tensor cores don't automatically accelerate attention due to softmax bottlenecks, and proposing Direct-P to work around this. The reported speedups (2.13× forward, 1.14× end-to-end) are modest and hardware-specific. The negative result on MXFP4 training is useful but the paper lacks comprehensive ablations, comparisons to other quantization strategies, and evaluation on models beyond 8B parameters. Reproducibility unclear—no mention of code release. Useful for practitioners optimizing on Blackwell but narrow applicability.
author: Robert Hu

title: The Head Complexity of Boolean Functions in Single-Layer Attention
summary: 단일 계층 self-attention에서 Boolean 함수를 계산하기 위해 필요한 최소 attention head 개수를 분석하며, k개 head는 k-bit parity를 계산할 수 있지만 (k+1)-bit parity는 계산할 수 없음을 증명한다.
reason: This paper provides a theoretical characterization of single-layer attention's computational capacity through the lens of head complexity. The main contribution—establishing that k heads compute k-bit parity but not (k+1)-bit parity—is a clean result with unconditional lower bounds that hold regardless of embedding dimension or precision. However, the practical relevance is limited: single-layer attention-only models are not how practitioners build systems, and the parity function, while theoretically natural, is not a capability practitioners care about optimizing. The compactness theorems are interesting but abstract. The paper makes a solid theoretical contribution to understanding attention mechanisms, but does not change what practitioners should build or how they should approach model design.
author: Rajmohan Rajaraman, Ravi Sundaram, Amanuel Tesfaye

title: Differentiable Hybrid Modelling for Learning and Optimising Chemical Transport Processes from Experimental Data
summary: JAX 기반의 미분 가능한 하이브리드 모델링 프레임워크를 제안하여 신경망 성분으로 구성 법칙을 학습하고 초기 조건을 맞추면서 화학 공정의 population balance equation을 모델링하고 최적화한다.
reason: A solid contribution combining differentiable programming with hybrid modelling for a specific chemical engineering problem. The work addresses real limitations (unknown constitutive laws, uncertain initial conditions) and demonstrates a practical framework integrating JAX with neural networks. However, the abstract provides limited evidence of empirical validation—no concrete performance comparisons, ablation studies, or quantitative results are reported. The scope is narrowed to population balance equations, and reproducibility details (code release, experimental datasets) are not mentioned. The idea of differentiable hybrid models is not new, though the application to this domain and the specific implementation appear competent. Without seeing actual experimental results or comparisons to baselines, it is difficult to assess whether this delivers the claimed improvements in prediction accuracy or optimization effectiveness.
author: Arthur Jessop, Mohammed Alsubeihi, Ben Moseley, Ashwin Kumar Rajagopalan

title: RobustSeiz: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking the Robustness of EEG Seizure Detection Models
summary: RobustSeiz는 임상적으로 동기부여된 분포 변화 하에서 EEG 발작 탐지기의 견고성을 평가하기 위한 오픈소스 벤치마킹 프레임워크로, 네 개의 공개 데이터셋을 표준화하고 노이즈 및 적대적 변환에 대한 체계적인 스트레스 테스트를 제공한다.
reason: A solid contribution that addresses a real problem in medical AI deployment—robustness evaluation of seizure detectors under realistic conditions. The framework is open-source, standardizes multiple datasets, and provides clinically motivated stress tests. However, the paper appears to be primarily a framework/benchmark release rather than a novel method or surprising empirical finding. The evaluation demonstrates the framework's utility but does not present breakthrough results or invalidate common assumptions. The work would be valuable for practitioners building seizure detection systems, but the impact is narrower than a method that changes how models should be built or deployed more broadly.
author: Mohammad Mohammadi, Alireza Zarei

title: Temporal Self-Distillation: Learning Visual State Tracking in Videos Without Supervision
summary: S³T는 시간적 샘플링 밀도를 특권 정보로 활용하여 비디오 상태 추적을 자기지도학습으로 학습하는 프레임워크로, 라벨 없이 모델이 자신의 학습 신호를 생성한다.
reason: A reasonable contribution with a novel self-supervised approach to video state tracking. The core idea—using temporal sampling density as privileged information for self-distillation—is intuitive and appears sound. However, the evaluation is limited: improvements are modest (1.74–2.70 points on VSTAT), tested on only one base model (LLaVA-OneVision-2-8B), and lacks comparison to supervised or other self-supervised baselines. The transfer results (+7.95 on VSTAT-YouTube, +4.50 on MVBench) are more compelling but still narrow in scope. No code or weights appear to be released. The work addresses a real problem (video understanding without labels) but the evidence does not yet support claims of broad practical impact.
author: Shravan Venkatraman, Wenshuai Zhao, Mohammad Hassan Vali, Arno Solin

title: TokenMatch: 3D Mesh Correspondence Transformer with Curvature-Guided Tokenisation
summary: TokenMatch는 곡률 기반 토큰화를 활용한 트랜스포머 모델로 부분적이고 비등거리 변형된 3D 메시 간의 대응을 추정하며, 여러 벤치마크에서 기존 방법을 능가하고 서브초 추론 속도를 달성한다.
reason: TokenMatch presents a solid contribution to 3D shape correspondence with a reasonable technical approach (curvature-guided tokenization for transformer-based matching) and evaluation across multiple benchmarks. However, the abstract lacks specific quantitative comparisons to strong baselines, making it difficult to assess the magnitude of improvements. The claim of generalizing from partial to full shapes without retraining is interesting but needs concrete evidence. The work is competent and addresses a real problem, but does not present a breakthrough result that would change practitioner decisions.
author: Adeela Islam, Zorah Lähner, Vittorio Murino, Vladislav Golyanik

title: Puffin-World: Scaling a Unified Multimodal Model with Native 3D World States
summary: Puffin-World는 물리, 기하, 외형을 통합하는 멀티모달 아키텍처를 제안하며, 1500만 개의 비전-언어-카메라 삼중쌍으로 구성된 Puffin-16M 데이터셋을 공개한다.
reason: A solid contribution with an interesting unified architecture for 3D world modeling, but the evaluation is limited. The abstract claims integration of physics, geometry, and appearance without external modules, and introduces a large dataset (Puffin-16M). However, no quantitative results, baselines, or comparisons are provided in the abstract. The novelty of jointly modeling these three world states is modest—each component (physics simulation, depth estimation, image generation) is well-explored. The claim of 'scaling' relies on dataset size rather than demonstrated performance gains. Code and dataset release is valuable for reproducibility, but without evidence of superior performance or novel capabilities over existing approaches, the contribution remains incremental. The work may be useful for practitioners building 3D world models, but the abstract does not establish why this particular unified approach is preferable to modular alternatives.
author: Kang Liao, Yihang Luo, Xiao-Ming Wu, Linyi Jin, Size Wu

title: Beyond Retrieval: Progressive Latent Memory Evolution for Streaming Video Understanding
summary: LatentStream는 스트리밍 비디오 이해를 위해 외부 메모리 뱅크 기반 검색 방식을 대신해 쿼리 관련 증거를 내부 잠재 메모리로 점진적으로 통합하는 프레임워크를 제안하며, 계층적 메모리 구성, 확장 가능한 수용 필드를 가진 잠재 토큰, 신뢰도 기반 최적화를 통해 스트리밍 추론을 개선한다.
reason: A solid contribution to streaming video understanding with a clear technical approach (latent memory evolution vs. store-and-retrieve), but the abstract lacks concrete performance numbers, baseline comparisons, or evidence of how substantial the improvements are. The method is well-motivated and the three-component design appears thoughtful, but without quantitative results or reproducibility signals (code/weights), it reads as a reasonable incremental advance rather than a must-read result. The problem is relevant to practitioners building video understanding systems, but the evaluation evidence presented is insufficient to judge impact.
author: Hongyu Qu, Guangming Yao, Ling Xing, Xiaobin Hu, Rongxing Ding

title: BooM-VVT: Boosting Mask-Free Video Virtual Try-On with Image-Level Pseudo Data
summary: BooM-VVT는 이미지 수준의 의사 데이터를 활용하여 마스크 없는 비디오 가상 피팅을 구현하며, 의류 민감 키프레임 샘플링과 Frame-Shared 3D-RoPE를 통해 의류 일관성과 시공간 대응을 개선하고, 다양한 카메라 시점을 지원하는 OmniView 데이터셋을 제시한다.
reason: A solid contribution to video virtual try-on with reasonable technical novelty (mask-free approach via image-level pseudo data, garment-sensitive keyframe sampling, Frame-Shared 3D-RoPE). The paper addresses real practical challenges (mask dependency, garment consistency, multi-view diversity) and introduces a new dataset (OmniView). However, the abstract does not provide quantitative comparisons to strong baselines, ablation details, or evidence of the claimed superiority. The work is incremental within the try-on domain rather than introducing a fundamentally new capability. Reproducibility depends on whether code and dataset are released (not confirmed in abstract).
author: Wei Zhang, Xin Li, Peishu Shi, Jialin Gao, Xuekang Peng

title: The Shape of Time: Video-Token Contrast for Temporal Understanding in VideoLMs
summary: VideoLMs이 텍스트 생성 감독에만 의존하면서 실제 시간적 이해보다 객체나 장면 같은 지름길을 학습할 수 있다는 문제를 지적하고, 순서 보존 뷰와 재정렬된 반사실적 뷰를 Kendall tau 거리로 대조하는 표현 수준의 시간적 대조 목표인 VT-Contrast를 제안한다.
reason: The paper identifies a real problem—that VideoLMs may exploit shortcuts rather than learning genuine temporal understanding—and proposes a straightforward contrastive learning solution at the representation level. The approach is practical (no architectural changes, compatible with existing training) and shows improvements on temporal benchmarks. However, the abstract provides limited evidence of the magnitude of gains, lacks comparison to other temporal supervision methods, and does not establish that this is a critical bottleneck for practitioners. The contribution is solid but incremental: adding a contrastive objective to existing models rather than a fundamental insight or breakthrough result.
author: Yumeng Shi, Quanyu Long, Yin Wu, Wenya Wang

title: Efficient Semantic Understanding from Digital Foveation
summary: 생물학적 시각에서 영감을 받아 디지털 포비에이션(foveated perception)을 통해 의미론적 분할을 효율적으로 수행하는 경량 능동 시각 파이프라인을 제시하며, 단일 포비에이 관찰로 계산 비용 4.7%만 사용하면서 95.9% 정확도를 달성한다.
reason: A solid contribution with convincing efficiency gains and thoughtful evaluation methodology. The paper addresses a real problem (computational cost of dense segmentation) with a biologically-inspired approach and demonstrates substantial savings (4.7% computation for single fovea, 58.6% for scene-level) while maintaining high accuracy. However, the scope is somewhat narrow—it applies existing techniques (saliency detection, foveated vision, semantic accumulation) to a specific task rather than introducing fundamentally new methods. The evaluation is honest and includes useful object-level metrics beyond standard pixel-wise measures, but the work is primarily an engineering contribution showing that active vision can be efficient for segmentation. The practical value for practitioners building efficient vision systems is real but incremental.
author: Caterina Caccavella, Vittorio Fra, Andreas Ziegler, Giulia D'Angelo, Yulia Sandamirskaya

title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: LaPla는 Vision-Language Model의 이산적 추론과 자율주행의 연속적 제어 간의 간극을 해소하기 위해 VQ-VAE 기반 액션 토크나이저와 잠재 공간 정렬 계획을 결합한 VLA 프레임워크로, nuScenes에서 기존 방법 대비 15.52% 오류 감소와 AlpaSim 폐루프 평가에서 33.34 포인트 성공률 향상을 달성했다.
reason: A solid contribution to end-to-end autonomous driving that addresses a real technical problem—bridging discrete language understanding and continuous control—with a reasonable solution (latent-aligned planning via VQ-VAE). The evaluation shows meaningful improvements on nuScenes and AlpaSim, and the approach avoids quantization errors through direct latent projection rather than codebook lookup. However, the novelty is somewhat incremental: using VQ-VAE latents as a bridge between modalities is a natural idea, and the core technical contribution (action tokenizer + concurrent queries) is not deeply novel. The paper lacks comparison to some relevant baselines and does not demonstrate whether the approach generalizes beyond the tested benchmarks. The closed-loop improvements are encouraging but modest in scope. Reproducibility is unclear—no mention of code or model release.
author: Ruoyu Yao, Yusen Xie, Qingzhao Liu, Pei Liu, Zewei Yang

summary: ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini 등 주요 AI 모델 네 개가 거의 동시에 서비스 중단을 경험했다.
